title: [Kernel] [Triton] Memory optimization for awq_gemm and awq_dequantize, 2x throughput

experiments.name: awq_triton_dequantize_gemm
experiments.workload: Author ran benchmarks/benchmark_throughput.py --input-len 2048 --output-len 128 --quantization awq --model Qwen/Qwen2-7B-Instruct-AWQ, measuring end-to-end serving throughput of the AWQ Triton path before vs after the kernel memory optimization.
experiments.note: Diff rewrites awq_dequantize_kernel and awq_gemm_kernel to load each packed 4-bit weight/zero element ONCE then expand via tl.interleave/tl.broadcast_to, instead of re-loading with //8 index arithmetic (BLOCK_SIZE_X*8 offsets). This cuts redundant memory loads. Number source: PR body throughput table - AWQ Triton no-opt 13351.06 tok/s, with-opt 27783.36 tok/s (also 6.14 -> 12.77 req/s); ~2x, beating the AWQ CUDA path (25049 tok/s).

reported.scope: end-to-end benchmark_throughput.py serving run (Qwen2-7B-Instruct-AWQ, in 2048 / out 128) on GPU, so the number includes attention, sampling and scheduling, not only the two AWQ kernels
reported.scale_short: Author's 13351->27783 tok/s is whole-pipeline serving throughput on GPU; our microbench isolates only awq_dequantize/awq_gemm and cannot run Triton CUDA kernels on CPU. TO MAKE 1:1: on a CUDA box, time just awq_dequantize_kernel + awq_gemm_kernel on a fixed weight tile and report kernel tok/s or us/call, isolating them from the rest of the serving loop.
reported.scale_note: The ~2x is real for the AWQ Triton path and even overtakes the hand-written AWQ CUDA kernel, but it is reported as E2E serving throughput, so the isolated-kernel ratio will differ. The kernels are Triton/CUDA-only and not reproducible on our arm CPU microbench; direction and rough magnitude are genuine.

environment: reported-only: author's published numbers; measured arms pending on GPU box
